Inkarn8: First Pages

Download Now

A DARK FANTASY ROGUELITE INSIDE A CURSED SPELLBOOK

Every page is a room. Every chapter is a floor.
Choose your own adventure through a living dungeon where your choices shape the path ahead. Draw sigils to cast spells, embrace corruption, and rewrite your fate within the Codex.

A Preview to Inkarn8: The Cursed Codex

Inkarn8: First Pages is an in-development preview of Inkarn8: The Cursed Codex. Content and presentation may change before release.

YOUR FIRST PAGES ARE WAITING

Inkarn8: First Pages is a playable introduction to Inkarn8: The Cursed Codex, a dark fantasy roguelite set inside a living cursed spellbook.

Enter the Codex, learn to draw sigils with your magical quill, make your first choices, face your first enemies, then choose your class and take your first steps into Chapter 1.

Every page is a room. Every chapter is a floor. Every choice shapes your adventure.

IN FIRST PAGES

  • Draw sigils to cast spells
  • Learn Inkarn8's tactical turn-based combat
  • Make choices within the living Codex
  • Discover your first artifacts and encounters
  • Begin unlocking the mysteries of the Scriptorium

 

 

🖋️ We Want Your Feedback!

Thank you for playing the prologue! As we build Inkarn8: The Cursed Codex, your thoughts are incredibly valuable to us. Drop a comment below and let us know:

  • The Vibe & Framing: Did you enjoy the book aesthetic and dark atmosphere?
  • The Combat: How did the tactical turn-based gameplay feel to you?
  • The Concept: What caught your attention most about the general game idea?
  • The Polish: Did you encounter any confusing tutorial moments or bugs?

Ok, finished the tutorial/demo. I think the full game looks good, though hopefully the tutorial process is less laborious there– I don’t like it when tutorials force me to take game actions, especially bad ones.

Overall, I think the sigil drawing is fun, though it will slow down combat too much for some people, but I think that’s okay; a game doesn’t have to be for everyone. Although I think the balance is fine, the language used in the tutorial makes me think that you think reserves are hard to replenish, which is false because you can convert unspent blots to ink by default and there’s no time limit on fights so any weak enemy you can leave alive is a full replenishment of your reserves at the end of a fight provided you can heal at all (one negative healing trait is fine, but two stacks would prevent this).

Also the shield slam sigil doesn’t work currently (it does 0 damage when consuming shield as well)

This feedback is excellent thank you for taking the time to give our game another shot after your initial difficulties. Then coming back with this detailed feedback is great for a small team. We would love to get you in our discord as we move into our steam page launch and alpha demo of chapter 1.

Regarding stalling on weaker enemies to heal this is one consideration we have had with the original press the attack resolution and skip action phase. For class's themselves in the full game we have adjusted the resolution actions to be more thematic to each class. In addition to this later enemies and encounters may have scaling mechanics or page corruptions over time. I do think for early encounters I don't mind a bit of safety and stalling but should be balanced with risk vs reward, better loot drops etc.

chameleonman23 days ago(+1)

Very cool concept! I liked the storytelling approach and ink based combat. The stamping of the actions onto the wax adds a lot of flavor and immersion!

At the moment, the drawing aspect seems a bit decorative since there is not pressure that exists to interrupt your drawing focus. Other games I've played before with drawing spells were realtime and therefore had more pressure on the player. I still really enjoyed it though!

The quill and action resource is really creative along with the ink surge concept. I'm looking forward to how it's going to develop and interact with the rest of the game later.

The bookmarking bits were still a little confusing to me as I'm still not sure what effects on the pathing it really had?

I also think it would be cool if the environment outside of the book was a little interactable as well such as putting out the candle lights or some other things, maybe a bit similar to hearthstones boards.

Overall very much enjoyed this little demo and am looking forward to seeing it develop further!

YNG8 Studios23 days ago

Thank you for the kind words and the thoughtful feedback, really appreciate it!

First Pages is very much a preview of the concept and is deliberately quite on rails. A lot of the things you've picked up on, including the world around the book, the desk and the wider Scriptorium, are intended to become much more interactive in the full game.

The bookmarks also become much more important once the Codex opens up. Each run the book changes and adapts, and bookmarks let you mark pages/rooms you may want to find your way back to. That's where the choose-your-own-adventure side of Inkarn8 really starts to come into play. Unfortunately, as you noticed, that doesn't have much opportunity to shine in this short preview.

The point about drawing pressure is interesting too and definitely something for us to think about as we expand the combat systems.

From your suggestions, it sounds like you're really getting what we're trying to build. We'd love to have you join us on Discord, help shape the game with feedback like this, and potentially get access to testing the Chapter 1 demo as we develop it!
